documents.name: Archify
documents.description: Use Archify with coding agents to create interactive architecture diagrams. Learn installation choices, source evidence, CLI validation and HTML delivery.
documents.introduction:
## What is Archify?

[Archify](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify) is an open-source agent skill that turns a description, plan or codebase into an interactive HTML diagram. The official project supports Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode.

Its useful distinction is an editable, typed source plus a generated viewer. You can refine a component or path in conversation and keep the underlying diagram source for later changes. This guide follows the official README checked October 31, 2026; it does not claim that an AI-generated architecture map is automatically accurate.

## Install or try the skill

Use the installation guidance linked from the official repository and [archify.si](https://archify.si). The README documents this temporary Codex trial:

```bash
npx skills use tt-a1i/archify@archify --agent codex
```

For a persistent installation, select your actual coding tool and review the proposed installation scope and files. The documented locations differ by host: for example, Codex uses an agents skills directory, while Claude Code uses a Claude skills directory.

The README identifies stable version 3.2.0 at the time checked. An installed copy can differ from the latest repository, so record the version used when sharing a reproducible example.

## Give the agent a bounded question

Start with one interaction you need to explain. For example, ask the agent to draw a browser request through an API, then a cache hit or database fallback. State that this is an illustrative design unless you have code or traces supporting it.

For a repository-derived map, specify:

- The service, directory or entry point to inspect.
- The primary request or workflow to show.
- The external services and trust boundaries that matter.
- Which relationships are confirmed and which remain uncertain.

Ask for a small high-level view before adding implementation detail. Verify the components and connections against the source rather than treating a visually polished diagram as evidence.

Archify offers an optional evidence-backed architecture mode with source links pinned to a public commit. Ordinary diagrams do not automatically contain those links. Choose the evidence mode deliberately if a reviewer needs to trace a claim back to code.

## Choose architecture, sequence or workflow

Use an architecture diagram for components and boundaries. Use a sequence diagram for one exchange over time, including returns and fallback. Use a workflow for steps, branches, approvals or recovery.

The project also documents data-flow, lifecycle, ERD, class, tree, timeline and waterfall views. Pick the form that answers the question instead of placing every concept on one canvas.

For timeline and waterfall views, distinguish measured timestamps and durations from illustrative values. A diagram generator cannot establish runtime timing without input evidence.

## Validate and deliver from a checkout

The repository includes a Node-based CLI. From its documented `archify` subdirectory, the README provides this example:

```bash
node bin/archify.mjs validate workflow examples/agent-tool-call.workflow.json --quality showcase --json
node bin/archify.mjs deliver workflow examples/agent-tool-call.workflow.json /tmp/workflow.html --quality showcase --open --json
```

These paths belong to a repository checkout; they are not universal paths inside every host's installed skill. Adjust the output path for your system.

Validation checks the typed source and rendering constraints. Delivery renders and checks a candidate before replacing the last known good artifact. Inspect diagnostics when validation fails, then review the resulting diagram visually.

A passing validator establishes compliance with its checks. It does not prove that the authored topology matches production, that a proposed change is safe to merge or that a drawn dependency exists.

## Share the artifact and its evidence

The output is a self-contained HTML file with exploration controls. The README documents focus, authored upstream/downstream reach, route inspection, presentation controls and exports.

Keep the typed source alongside the delivered artifact when the diagram must be maintained. Include the repository revision or the date of the input evidence in the accompanying explanation.

Hosted sharing, automatic Mermaid parsing and general-purpose WYSIWYG editing are outside the project's documented scope. If a workflow requires those capabilities, confirm a separate tool or service before adopting it.

## License and costs

Current project source is Apache-2.0 licensed. The official website supplies information, examples and installation guidance; similarly named paid services are not automatically affiliated with the project.

Your coding agent or model provider may have separate fees and data-handling terms. The open-source license does not include those services.

For reviewing the interface of a generated tool, see [Impeccable](https://findryai.com/item/impeccable). Browse [Developer Tools](https://findryai.com/category/developer-tools) for related software.

## Official source

- [Archify README: installation, diagram types, CLI workflow, scope and licensing](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify)

Documentation checked October 31, 2026. No local installation or generated-diagram accuracy benchmark was performed for this listing.

documents.name: Filee
documents.description: Convert files locally with Filee. Check platform support, optional engines and CLI JSON results before preparing documents, images or audio for AI workflows.
documents.introduction:
## What is Filee?

[Filee](https://github.com/KnifeLemon/Filee) is a free, MIT-licensed desktop file converter with a drag-and-drop interface and a command-line tool. It covers documents, images, media and structured data, with some conversions requiring optional engines.

It can help prepare files for AI workflows: for example, extracting readable document text, converting images or producing local transcription output. It is primarily a conversion utility, rather than a general AI assistant.

This guide follows the official README, engine documentation and agent integration instructions checked October 31, 2026. Conversion quality and performance were not independently tested.

## Download the correct platform package

Start at the repository's [official releases](https://github.com/KnifeLemon/Filee/releases/latest).

The README documents Windows 10/11 installer and portable options, Linux x64/ARM64 packages, and a macOS 13+ preview. Select the package for your operating system and architecture.

Linux drag gestures require X11; the documentation directs Wayland users to the drop zone and file-manager context menu. The macOS preview is not notarized. Check the current release notes and signing information before installing rather than assuming identical platform support.

The app's drag workflow holds Ctrl, or Option on macOS, while dragging files, then drops them on a suitable target format. The menu shows applicable conversions rather than every format for every input.

## Check the conversion route before running it

The command-line tool shares engines and presets with the app. First check that it is available:

```bash
filee version
filee formats md --json
```

The official agent instructions distinguish two lists in the formats response:

- `targets`: outputs available with the current installation.
- `withEngines`: outputs requiring an additional engine.

If the desired output is in neither list, do not assume the conversion is supported. If an engine is missing, open Settings → Engines and inspect the named dependency before retrying.

On Linux and macOS, the documented command link is under the user's local bin directory, which must be on PATH. On Windows, the integration instructions also describe invoking the CLI from the Filee installation folder.

## Make outputs easy to verify

For a first image conversion:

```bash
filee convert photo.png --to jpg -o converted --json
```

Choose a small sample and an explicit output folder. Review the resulting file before processing a larger collection, especially when transparency, image quality, page layout or metadata matters.

The official integration instructions say that exit code 0 alone does not prove every input was converted. Read the JSON:

- Check the `converted`, `skipped` and `failed` totals.
- Inspect each `files[].state`.
- Use the exact paths in `files[].outputs`.

An input is converted when its state is `done` and its output list is nonempty. A skipped input has not just been converted. Exit code 1 indicates failures or cancellations; 2 indicates bad arguments or a missing input; 3 indicates nothing to convert.

Filee normally adds a number instead of overwriting an existing output. Its documented flags include `--skip` and `--overwrite`; choose deliberately when integrating it with a script or agent.

## Know which engine does the work

The engine documentation distinguishes built-in conversions from optional downloads. Examples include Pandoc for additional markup routes, FFmpeg for audio/video, and Tesseract for OCR.

For document preparation, distinguish text extraction from recognition. The built-in PDF text path extracts existing text without OCR. A scanned page needs an OCR route; converting it to an image does not make its text searchable.

The documented PDF-to-PPTX route places a picture of each page on a slide, with text in speaker notes. It does not promise fully editable slide objects.

Filee also documents optional Windows-only local speech transcription using Whisper, with FFmpeg required. Confirm the current platform and engine availability before designing a workflow around it. A supported media format does not itself establish that transcription is installed.

## Local conversion and network activity

The project states that conversion runs on your computer without uploading the files and that it sends no usage telemetry. That is the maintainer's documented policy, not an independent network audit.

Offline conversion is separate from obtaining dependencies. The app checks GitHub for updates and can download selected engines or OCR language files. The update check can be disabled in Settings → About.

Browser links are downloaded without the browser's signed-in session. Do not expect a protected download link to work merely because it opens in an authenticated browser tab.

## A practical place in an AI workflow

Use Filee as a preparation step, then inspect the outputs before sending them to another tool. For a document pipeline, verify text completeness and reading order; for structured data, check the shape of the exported table; for media, confirm duration and synchronization.

Local conversion does not determine what a later AI service uploads or retains. Review the next tool's behavior separately.

For AI-assisted video editing after preparation, see [Concat](https://findryai.com/item/concat). Browse [Developer Tools](https://findryai.com/category/developer-tools) for related automation utilities.

## Official sources

- [Filee README: downloads, platform support, interface, CLI and privacy policy](https://github.com/KnifeLemon/Filee)
- [Conversion engines and route limitations](https://github.com/KnifeLemon/Filee/blob/main/docs/ENGINES.md)
- [Official agent instructions: JSON fields, exit codes and output verification](https://github.com/KnifeLemon/Filee/blob/main/skills/filee/SKILL.md)

Documentation checked October 31, 2026. No conversion or transcription test was performed for this listing.
